discovery: Spherical-aberration correction in electron optics, enabling sub-ångström transmission electron microscopy

nominees.name: Harald Rose
nominees.affiliation: Technische Universität Darmstadt / Universität Ulm, Germany

subfield: Condensed matter and materials physics / electron optics and microscopy
motivation: Scherzer showed in 1936 that round electron lenses always have spherical aberration, and for sixty years this limited TEM resolution well above interatomic distances. Harald Rose designed a practical hexapole corrector. In 1997–98 Maximilian Haider built it and Knut Urban's group demonstrated it on a working transmission electron microscope, overcoming the Scherzer limit. Aberration-corrected TEM and STEM are now standard instruments worldwide. They image individual atomic columns, light elements, interfaces, dopants and defects directly, and with quantitative contrast. This has changed condensed-matter and materials physics. It has revealed the atomic structure of strengthening precipitates in alloys, of oxide heterointerfaces, of 2D materials, and of catalysts and battery materials, which guides the design of real materials in industry. The work is a key physics invention, grounded in rigorous electron-optical theory and precise engineering, and its impact is broad and lasting.
